witness.note: a stripped gcc 9.4 QuickJS interpreter; JSValue is { JSValueUnion u; int64_t tag; }, sixteen bytes, returned in RAX:RDX

decisions: The need was filed with an EMPTY hypothesis, so there was no filed diagnosis to overturn. The cause found: FuncCallSpecs::buildOutputFromTrials (fspec.cc:5777) handles one used output trial; upstream handles two; kuna shipped the multi-trial arm as STUB(W4 translate-on-handle). The cspec output rule had already put two active trials on the call, so the call got no output at all and both INDIRECT creations survived as locals nothing assigns.
The parameter asserts in the probe are a red herring: the symptom is byte-identical with no --assert at all. They neither cause nor mask the defect.

NOT a new mechanism. kuna_rustabi (DIV-136) already completed this arm with a sound, language-agnostic classification (model rule + both halves read + a one-sided callee-body veto) and then gated it on Compiler::Rustc, which a GCC image can never satisfy. `--option rustabi always` closes the acceptance today; it is not a default-flip candidate because `always` also drops the language test for the PRODUCER-side rule, which is why rustabi ships off. The fix is to split the consumer half out behind its own gate.

Default ON: the arm only ever ADDS a definition -- two INDIRECT creations become two SUBPIECEs of a value the CALL now produces. No statement can be removed that was not a read of an undefined local, and no call can lose an argument. Measured on 498 images, this held with no exceptions.

The reach is the cspec's output model, not an architecture list: <join_dual_class/> on x86-64 System V and MIPS64, and the plain <join/> over r0/r1 on 32-bit ARM -- which is how every soft-float double comes back from __aeabi_dmul. The ARM half was found by a stage-test regression, not by design, and the sweep was widened to 93 ARM/MIPS images because of it.

Widening seed_callee_return_writes so this option's veto keeps its evidence exposed a pre-existing latent coupling: seed_callee_preserves is gated on `calleepreserves`, so the default-ON `calleeretpreserves` was silently dead whenever `calleepreserves` was off. Under default options the widening is a strict no-op (calleepreserves already seeds every direct call). tests/stages/kuna-calleepreserves.xml now holds BOTH rules off in its off pass, because either one closes its witness.

sweep.method: kuna decompile-all, --option callretpair off vs default, whole-binary text compared
sweep.corpora: 398 decbench C builds (O0/O2/O2-noinline) + 11 RE-dataset x86-64 ELFs + 93 ARM/MIPS images (decbench Cortex-M firmware, RE-dataset ARM crackmes, kuna-analysis ARM/MIPS/PPC fixtures)
sweep.witness_image: 422 of 1587 functions changed; never-assigned locals 3304 -> 1688 (-48.9%); emitted C 89520 -> 88183 lines
sweep.statement_drops_read_individually: 43 functions; every one the same collapse, `f(); v4 = v3; return v4;` -> `return f();`
sweep.elsewhere: coreutils make-prime-list process_prime stores the halves of __udivti3's 128-bit quotient instead of two undefined locals; newlib scalbn on ARM returns __aeabi_dmul(...) instead of CONCAT44 of two phantoms (17 never-assigned locals -> 5)
